title: bug: under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 the wrappers still find node/python3 by PATH lookup, so a project-local ./node or ./python3 reachable through a cwd PATH entry runs
description: Found by task-aa85ff13 (protected agent CLI). moe-agent.sh find_node (`command -v node`, then line ~95 prepends `dirname` of it to PATH) and find_python (`command -v python3`) use PATH lookup even with MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1. With an empty, '.' or relative PATH entry and cwd = project, a repository-planted ./node or ./python3 becomes the wrapper's helper runtime (and `dirname ./node` puts '.' first on PATH). The ps1 twin runs `node` by name. Fix shape: under the marker, apply aa85ff13's trusted-PATH rule (absolute, outside the project's real path) to node/python3 (or filter PATH once at the top), with sh+ps1 rows like scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development. Re-anchor on the LANDED bytes at claim time: aa85ff13 landed as aae40eb0, and later wrapper-lane rows may have moved lines. Anchor on names, never line numbers: sh refuse_protected_agent, protected_resolve_cli, find_node, find_python, parse_command_into_argv; ps1 Stop-MoeProtectedAgent, Get-MoeRealPath, Resolve-MoeProtectedCli, $script:MoeProtectedCli (mem:task-task-aa85ff13a8894913ae34242dbab6f395-handoff).

Extend aa85ff13's harness in scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs; do not fork it.
- run() takes an `env` option applied last; a key set to undefined is deleted, so a row can drop MOE_NODE_COMMAND.
- run() appends the fixture's node-only dir (dirname(fx.node), POSIX only) to every row's PATH unless the row passes nodeDir:false. This keeps aa85ff13's ps1 rows resolving node on a pwsh host whose /usr/bin and /bin hold no node. Its sh rows already get node through MOE_NODE_COMMAND.
- Planted interpreters: cliStub node, and python3 on sh rows, into the project root and project/bin with where='project' (Windows: node.cmd). N2 on Windows also copies a small System32 exe to project\bin\node.exe, so a wrong pick shows in the OK line.
- Refusal rows build sys/ outside the project: symlinks to every entry of /usr/bin and /bin except node and python3 (POSIX). The wrapper's ordinary tools still run, but no trusted interpreter exists. Windows refusal rows use TAIL without dirname(process.execPath).
- Constants: interpreterNotFound(name) = `[ERROR] MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND: ${name} was not found on an absolute PATH entry outside the project; refusing to start.` OK lines, ANSI stripped: sh `[OK] Using node: <file> (<process.version>)` and `[OK] Using python3: <file>`; ps1 `[OK] Using node: <file>`. Expected files are a realpath'd dir plus the name, matching pwd -P and Get-MoeRealPath.

Rows. Names are engine-prefixed; ps1 rows skip where PowerShell is absent, as today.
- N1 [sh, ps1]: for each of an empty, '.' and relative 'bin' entry placed FIRST, with MOE_NODE_COMMAND dropped and PATH [entry, empty, nodebin (POSIX), trusted, ...TAIL]:

  - An absolute file in another outside dir (altnode/node) is used.
  - With it dropped, Moe's managed runtime $HOME/.local/share/moe/node/current/bin/node (a symlink to process.execPath under fx.home) is used ahead of PATH.
- N4 [sh, ps1]: refusal for each planted entry kind when no trusted node exists (sys/ or TAIL without node; MOE_NODE_COMMAND dropped): assertRefused(engine, fx, r, interpreterNotFound('node')).
- P1 [sh]: python3 refusal. node is trusted via MOE_NODE_COMMAND=fx.node; python3 is only planted or in-project; PATH [entry, nodebin, sys]. assertRefused(..., interpreterNotFound('python3')).

  - The project gets .moe/daemon.json '{}'. MOE_PROXY_PATH is the runtime stub. PATH is ['.', nodebin, ...TAIL].

- L2 [sh, ps1]: legacy, with the marker unset and '01', MOE_NODE_COMMAND dropped, nothing planted, PATH [nodebin, trusted, ...TAIL].
  - sh prints the bare `[OK] Using node: node (...)` and `[OK] Using python3: python3`.
  - ps1 prints no 'Using node:' line.
  - There is no MOE_PROTECTED_ line, and the run reaches its first runtime call on its own.
- S1 static (no engine), on scripts/moe-agent.ps1 with full-line comments stripped:

Red proof: on the current wrappers N1-N4, P1, M1 and S1 fail and L2 passes; record which.

implementationPlan.description:

A refusal must run in the main shell, never inside $( ).

Keep the file parseable by bash 3.2 (mem:gotcha-bash32-heredoc-inside-comsub): no mapfile, no associative arrays, no heredoc inside $( ). (c) The find_python site. Under the marker, call protected_pin_interpreters in the main shell (it may exit); otherwise run `PYTHON_CMD=$(find_python)` as today. Both then fall through to the existing empty check and the `[OK] Using python3:` line. protected_pin_interpreters:
- project = $(normalize_path "$PROJECT"), the raw --project. It is empty under --project-name/--list-projects, which therefore fail closed.
- node is the first of these that qualifies:
  - MOE_NODE_COMMAND, when it starts with '/' and is an executable regular file whose dir passes protected_trusted_dir;
  - $HOME/.local/share/moe/node/current/bin/node, under the same test;

- If no node qualifies: refuse_protected_agent "[ERROR] MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND: node was not found on an absolute PATH entry outside the project; refusing to start."

- python3 = `protected_path_lookup python3`; otherwise the same refusal, naming python3.

The legacy fixed install dirs (/opt/homebrew/bin, nvm, volta, fnm) and `py -3`/`python` are not probed under the marker. A terminal launch has them on PATH; otherwise MOE_NODE_COMMAND names node.

implementationPlan.description:

(a) Extract the scan out of Resolve-MoeProtectedCli into Find-MoeProtectedFile([string]$Name, [string[]]$Extensions). It runs the same loop and returns the file or $null: absolute entries only, Get-MoeRealPath, the in-project skip with the same comparison, the untrimmed [IO.Path]::Combine, Test-Path -PathType Leaf. (b) Pin node just before `$script:MoeProtectedCli = $null`, so node refuses before the CLI, as in sh.
- Set `$script:MoeNode = $null`.
- Under the marker, set `$script:MoeNode = Find-MoeProtectedFile 'node'` with @('.exe') on Windows, else @(''). Only node.exe counts on Windows, because Start-Process, ProcessStartInfo and an MCP config can launch only an executable.
- If it is $null, call Stop-MoeProtectedAgent with the MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND line for node, byte-identical to sh.
- Otherwise run `Set-Alias -Name node -Value $script:MoeNode -Scope Script` and `Write-Host "[OK] Using node: $script:MoeNode"`.

(c) Every `& node` call keeps its text. Aliases outrank applications, so under the marker each one runs the pinned file: Invoke-MoeRpc and Invoke-MoeRpcRaw, the usage and prompt-cache helpers, the account helper, the worktree and git-guard programs, the claude stream. The launcher tests that execute ps1 slices (usage-launcher, seat-registration, moe-account-lease, prompt-cache-launcher) keep running node from PATH with no preamble change.

(d) The sites an alias cannot reach read $script:MoeNode; $null keeps the legacy 'node' byte for byte.

- The codex-stream ProcessStartInfo: add `if ($script:MoeNode) { $psi.FileName = $script:MoeNode }` on the line after it is built. .NET's Process.Start('node') searches the current directory, the project, before PATH. The line is null-safe inside the prompt-cache-launcher and usage-launcher slices.

- The codex and grok TOML `command`, with .Replace('\', '/') like $proxyScriptForToml. Get-CodexMoeServerOverride re-emits it unchanged.
- The heartbeat Start-Job, a separate process: $pin gains `Node = [string]$script:MoeNode`, and the job body begins `if ($Pin.Node) { Set-Alias -Name node -Value $Pin.Node }`.

Error handling: the refusal exits 1 before any MCP config, daemon start, proxy RPC or CLI, like aa85ff13's.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
With MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED exactly '1', scripts/moe-agent.sh pins node and python3, and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 pins node, to absolute files chosen by aa85ff13's trusted-PATH rule: the first absolute PATH entry whose real path is neither the project's real path nor under it. sh also accepts an absolute MOE_NODE_COMMAND, then Moe's managed runtime, under the same directory rule. ps1 takes only node.exe on Windows.

Every later launch uses the pinned file: wrapper RPCs and helpers, the MCP configs handed to the agent CLI, and the heartbeat job. In sh this includes moe-call.sh's deregister, which no longer probes python3 under the marker. Nothing reachable only through an empty, '.', relative or in-project PATH entry ever runs.

When no trusted interpreter exists, the wrapper exits 1 before any MCP config write, daemon start, RPC or CLI. It prints `[ERROR] MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND: <name> was not found on an absolute PATH entry outside the project; refusing to start.` to stderr; for node the line is byte-identical in both twins. Without the marker, behaviour and output are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: N1 [sh, ps1]: an empty, '.' or relative entry is placed first. A planted node (sh: and python3) in the project root and project/bin never runs, through pre-flight, the first runtime call and the exit deregister. The [OK] lines name the trusted absolute files, and the claude MCP config's moe command is the pinned node.

N2 [sh, ps1]: an in-project absolute PATH entry is skipped whether it is spelled directly, through a link or through '..'. N3 [sh]: MOE_NODE_COMMAND counts only as an absolute executable in a trusted dir, and the managed runtime is used ahead of PATH.

N4 [sh, ps1] and P1 [sh]: when no trusted node (or python3) exists, the run exits 1 with exactly the MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND line on stderr. No stub ran, no runtime call was made and no MCP config was written.

M1 [sh]: moe-call.sh under the marker never runs a planted python3. L2 [sh, ps1]: without the marker (unset, '01'), sh prints the bare legacy names, ps1 prints no node line, there is no MOE_PROTECTED_ line, and the run reaches its first runtime call. aa85ff13's rows stay green.
S1: moe-agent.ps1 keeps no node launch literal outside the $script:MoeNode and alias paths.
The step-6 verification command exits 0, and its PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7 rows run under node.exe rather than being skipped.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Filter PATH once at the top (the description's alternative). Rejected. moe-agent.sh picks node before argument parsing and python3 before the project is canonicalised, so the in-project half of the rule cannot be applied there. An absolute in-project entry, such as an IDE-activated <project>/.venv/bin, would still win before the project is known. Dropping such entries would also strip the agent CLI's own environment.
2. ps1: replace every `& node` with an explicit `& $script:MoeNode`. Rejected. Several launcher tests (usage-launcher, seat-registration, moe-account-lease) execute ps1 slices holding `& node`, and each would need a preamble edit, pushing the plan to 7+ files. A script-scope alias reaches every in-process `& node` with no text change. Only the six non-command sites read $script:MoeNode. $script:MoeNode is null unless protected, which is aa85ff13's $script:MoeProtectedCli pattern, so the codex-stream FileName override stays null-safe inside its two test slices.
3. A separate row for moe-call.sh. Folded in instead: a protected sh seat's EXIT-trap deregister is the wrapper running moe-call.sh, whose python3 probe ran a planted ./python3. The fix is a few lines.
4. Export MOE_NODE_COMMAND for moe-call.sh. Unnecessary: use_node already puts the pinned node's dir first on PATH.
5. A new refusal code vs reusing MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI_NOT_FOUND. A new code, MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND: it is distinct from the agent CLI and still matches aa85ff13's 'MOE_PROTECTED_' test filter only on refusal rows. Success prints the existing [OK] lines, so aa85ff13's exact-line assertions stay intact.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
sh ordering:
- find_node runs at the top, before argument parsing. Its dir is prepended to PATH, and `dirname ./node` yields '.'.
- aa85ff13's command gate runs before parse_command_first_token. That call runs `${PYTHON_CMD:-python3}` (python3 bare, PYTHON_CMD unset) for shlex.
- find_python runs after CLI detection.
- PROJECT is canonicalised later (normalize_path, then cd/pwd).
- `"$NODE_CMD" prompt-cache check` runs before the R13c2 gate and protected_resolve_cli.
- bash `command -v node` returns './node' for an empty or '.' entry and 'bin/node' for a relative one (probed).

ps1:
- It never uses python or moe-call.sh.
- node runs at about 13 `& node` sites. It also runs at Start-Process -FilePath "node" (daemon autostart), ProcessStartInfo('node') (codex exec stream), the claude and gemini MCP JSON, the codex and grok TOML, and inside the heartbeat Start-Job, a separate process that sees no script variables.
- Command precedence is alias > function > cmdlet > application.
- .NET Process.Start with a bare name searches the current directory before PATH (Windows CreateProcess, and .NET's Unix ResolvePath).

moe-call.sh:
- It probes python3 and node before its R13c2 block.
- PYTHON_CMD's only reader is find_proxy's install-path fallback.

Tests:
- agent-runtime.test.mjs runs sh --help with a stub-only PATH and requires the legacy node line. prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs slices parse_command_into_argv through CLI detection.
- The protected test fixture realpaths its root, so pwd -P outputs match.
planningNotes.risks:
- The codex-stream ProcessStartInfo and the codex, gemini and grok config writers are not reached by the rows. S1 pins them statically; review them by hand.
- PYTHON_CMD is expanded unquoted at many sites (legacy 'py -3'). A trusted python3 path containing whitespace would break those sites. It is out of scope and practically absent on supported hosts.
- MSYS python3.exe may be the WindowsApps stub. MSYS is not a JetBrains protected launch path.
- A rejected MOE_NODE_COMMAND is skipped silently. The [OK] line shows the chosen node.
- --project-name and --list-projects fail closed under the marker: there is no project to be outside of before the registry lookup. The JetBrains launcher always passes --project.
- Refusal precedence differs between the twins only when several protected requirements fail at once. The sh pin runs before its R13c2 file checks; in ps1 the pin runs after them.
- Residuals, not fixed here, flagged on the epic-final row:
  - other tools (git, dirname, uname, serena) still resolve by PATH under the marker;
  - a standalone moe-call.sh under the marker finds node by PATH;
  - on Windows, npm .cmd shims and cmd.exe search the cwd before PATH for `node` (NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath).
- Docs: the TROUBLESHOOTING rows for MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND and aa85ff13's two codes belong to f3f364a6's docs sweep (step 2).
- Lane: this row edits moe-agent.sh/.ps1, the serialized wrapper lane. The governor sets its slot. Never edit while another seat's harness runs the live wrapper.
